'''Walter Laws Smith''' (November 12, 1926 – March 6, 2023) was a British-born American mathematician, known for his contributions to applied [[probability theory]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Walter Smith Obituary {{!}} UNC Statistics & Operations Research |url=https://stor.unc.edu/news-item/walter-smith-obituary/ |access-date=2023-04-22 |website=stor.unc.edu}}</ref>

==Biography==
Smith was born in London on November 12, 1926.<ref name="google">{{cite journal|title=American Men and Women of Science: The physical and biological sciences|author=Jaques Cattell Press|journal=American Men & Women of Science|date=1982|issue=v. 6; v. 15, no. 6|publisher=Bowker|issn=0192-8570|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=L5QeAAAAMAAJ|accessdate=2015-04-14}}</ref>

Smith received a B.A. in [[mathematics]] (1947) from [[Cambridge University]], having gained First Class in the Mathematical Tripos Part 1 and Part 2. He then received an M.A. (1951) and Ph.D. (1953) from Cambridge. His dissertation was entitled ''Stochastic Sequences of Events'' advised by [[Henry Daniels (statistician)|Henry Daniels]] and [[David Cox (statistician)|D. R. Cox]], with whom he published the book ''Queues'' (1961) and also published with in his early years.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=13420}}</ref>  He became a professor of statistics at The [[University of North Carolina]] Chapel Hill (1954–56 and 1958–), and he was an [[emeritus]] professor in the Department of Statistics and Operations Research.<ref>[http://www.stat.unc.edu/faculty/wsmith.html homepage] at unc.edu</ref>

Smith was a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] (1966), a winner of the [[Adams Prize]] at the University of Cambridge (1960), a Sir Winston Churchill overseas fellow and a recipient of a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (see [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1974]])

Smith died in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]], on March 6, 2023, at the age of 96.<ref>{{cite web |title=Walter Laws Smith |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/newsobserver/name/walter-smith-obituary?id=50502227 |website=Legacy |access-date=19 March 2023}}</ref>

==Publications==
*''The superimposition of several strictly periodic sequences of events'', in [[Biometrika]], 40(?), 1953. With Cox.
*''A direct proof of a fundamental theorem of renewal theory'', in [[Skandinavisk Aktuartidsskrift]], 36(?), 1953
*''On the superposition of renewal processes'', in [[Biometrika]], 41(1–2):91–99, 1954. With Cox.
*''A note on truncation and sufficient statistics'' in [[The Annals of Mathematical Statistics]], 28(1):247–252, 1957
*''On the distribution of Tribolium confusum in a container'', in [[Biometrika]], 44(?), 1957. With Cox.
*''[https://www.jstor.org/stable/2983891 Renewal theory and its ramifications]'', in [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society]], 20(2):243–302, 1958
*''On the elementary renewal theorem for non-identically distributed variables'', in [[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]], 14(2):673–699, 1964
*''Congestion Theory'', Proceedings of the Symposium on Congestion Theory, The University of North Carolina Monograph Series in Probability and Statistics., 1965. With [[William E. Wilkinson]] (editors).
*''Necessary conditions for almost sure extinction of a branching process with random environment'', [[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]],. 39(?):2136–2140, 1968
*''Branching processes in Markovian environments'' in [[Duke Mathematical Journal]] 38(4):749–763, 1971. With [[William E. Wilkinson]]
*''[[Harold Hotelling]] 1895–1973'' in [[The Annals of Statistics]], 6(6):1173–1183, 1978
*''On transient regenerative processes'' in [[Journal of Applied Probability]], 23(?):52–70, 1986. With E. Murphree.
